summary.headline: Coromandel Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell 3% YoY to INR761 crores on West Asia input-cost spike, while revenue rose 15% to INR8,215 crores.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income rose 15% YoY to INR8,215 crores, helped by higher fertilizer realisations and non-subsidy growth, with NACL now consolidated. EBITDA declined 3% to INR761 crores and net profit fell to INR382 crores from INR502 crores as ammonia and sulphur costs outran NBS subsidy rates. Management said phosphate production was deliberately cut to 6.9 lakh tons (72% utilisation) to protect inventory economics, while Crop Protection (revenue +20%, EBIT +44%) and Retail (revenue +85%) carried the quarter. Management is pressing the government for a kharif NBS revision and says no near-term fertilizer capacity additions are planned.

segments.name: Fertilizers (phosphatic)
segments.commentary: Production cut to 6.9 lakh tons from 8.4 lakh tons (72% utilisation) to optimise inventory; phos acid output 1.2 lakh tons, flat YoY. Sales volume fell 9-10% to 10 lakh tons, but primary market share rose to 22% from 18%; point-of-sale up 13% to 7.9 lakh tons, 16% share.

segments.name: Specialty nutrients and organics
segments.commentary: Described as strong, aided by higher organics and micronutrient offtake; launched 3 new products. Management says this business grows 25-30% with about 20% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Crop Protection
segments.commentary: Record Q1: revenue +20% to INR870 crores, EBIT +44% to INR159 crores, with exports and B2B strong. New products are 32% of domestic B2C sales vs 23% last year.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Revenue +85% YoY; 76% of stores profitable vs 61% last year; 22 new stores take network above 1,200 outlets.

segments.name: Nano and bio products
segments.commentary: Nano business volumes +2% YoY with nearly 60% market share; UP and Maharashtra bans are restraining growth. Bio business steady, with 2 new products launched.

guidance_outlook: Phosphoric acid price for Q2 settled at $1,700/t vs $1,360/t in Q1, following higher DAP and raw-material prices.
Granulation project on track for commissioning in Q4 FY27; Crop Protection capacity expansion for key molecules expected by September 2026.

Management wants kharif NBS rates revised to the 6-month average policy formula; says the industry has taken a 25-30% price increase across grades, and that further price rises are not feasible without subsidy correction.
Sulphur expected to stay high for some time; management says the acid-backed production economics are unattractive until sulphur falls, with NACL-type steady-state EBITDA well below Coromandel.

No near-term fertilizer capacity additions planned; target is 4 million tons own fertilizer plus 1 million tons trading, with management citing 8-9 million tons of nutrient visibility for about 2 years.
Normal sustainable capex guided at about INR300 crores per year; ~INR7,000 crores invested over the last 3-4 years.
capex_capacity: Phos acid and sulphuric acid plants commissioned; sulphuric acid at rated capacity and generating power; phos acid stabilising with a new rock-utilisation technology.
Granulation project on track for Q4 FY27 commissioning; new capacity is 750,000 tonnes, 50% to be sold via own retail and the balance into UP, Rajasthan, MP and Chhattisgarh.

Crop Protection key-molecule capacity to be commissioned by September 2026; further spending to focus on marketing and channel rather than assets; no new AI capacity planned given spare NACL capacity.
Senegal rock mining produced over 1.1 lakh tons in the quarter; BMCC operating close to 5 lakh tons/year target; evaluating a 100,000-150,000 ton SSP plant at $5-6 million.

Kakinada T-MAP plant and seaweed granulation plant progressing; Ankleshwar fluorination launch facility being set up; IIT Chennai research park planned; PA-SA plant gives about 60% acid self-sufficiency.
demand_pricing: Monsoon deficit was 23% through the quarter, moderating to 17% by late July; reservoirs at 34% of capacity vs 57% last year. Pulses acreage down 15%, oilseeds and cotton down 6%, and paddy back to normal.
Management says there is no fertilizer shortage; Urea and DAP stocks are comfortable for kharif, but industry production and imports must hold for two more months to build rabi carryover.
NP/NPK production and imports fell 21% and 38% respectively; management ties this to weak NBS subsidy for these grades.
Crop protection: domestic demand muted due to delayed sowing; export markets improving but cautious on price. Active ingredient prices are firmer than before because China keeps AIs low.
NACL export revenue hit by price moderation on molecules sold to global MNCs, while Coromandel passed input-cost increases through to exports.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a structural shift to NPK or a fertilizer shortage on the ground?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no shortage; the early-season pick-up of low-MRP packs was an advance purchase, and current uptake depends more on monsoon than on availability.

qa_highlights.question: How much did FX contribute to Crop Protection EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FX is at most 5-6% of consolidated EBITDA, under a netting-based hedging policy.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the depreciation spike and how much is from new capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental depreciation from new capex is about INR16-18 crores; the rest is mining overburden amortisation (about INR30 crores) and NACL intangibles amortisation (about INR20-21 crores).

qa_highlights.question: What is the ask from government and how is the EBITDA per ton outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wants the 6-month average NBS rate applied, and says NP/NPK rates need significant correction; the target is nutrient EBITDA of about INR6,500/t from INR5,000/t, but not in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for the next 1-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided normal sustainable capex of about INR300 crores, but will consider higher spending for attractive-return projects.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Dhaksha drone contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Coromandel bought 100-150 drones this quarter and targets a fleet of 500 during the year; management said Dhaksha is not a significant EBITDA drag.

risks_watch: Subsidy under-recovery on NP/NPK: sulphur and ammonia costs are not covered by NBS rates, and kharif revision is still pending.
Sulphur and phos acid pricing: phos acid up to $1,700/t in Q2; management says sulphur needs to fall to about $800/t for backward integration to pay.
Subsidy receivable of INR3,254 crores at June-end.
State bans on Nano fertilizers in UP and Maharashtra are holding back volumes.
Crop Protection export pricing: AI prices are firmer, but export demand is cautious and NACL revenue fell on price moderation.
Whether industry production and imports can hold through the next two months to build rabi carryover inventory.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the non-fertilizer businesses (Crop Protection, Retail, Specialty) but cautious and repeatedly pressing the government on fertilizer subsidy. Management was evasive on a few specifics (CP export/domestic mix, Dhaksha numbers, NACL stake increase), deferring them to follow-up.
key_quotes: Overall, we have delivered a resilient performance in a challenging operating environment marked by delayed monsoons, elevated raw material costs and pressure on fertilizer margins.
These rates do not fully compensate for the increase in global raw material costs, which happened subsequent to Middle East crisis.
Given the Phosphoric Acid price of $1,700, at least we want $800 of sulphur.
So I would put a normal sustainable capex of INR300 crores would be the number we'll look at.

growth.why: No explicit revenue growth guidance; phosphate volumes deliberately cut to 72% utilisation, with the 750,000 t granulation project due Q4 FY27 and Crop Protection key-molecule expansion due by September 2026, while management says no near-term fertilizer capacity additions are planned and the kharif NBS revision is still being pressed for.
